versioning_policy.description: This project uses a semver-like X.Y.Z format. Each bucket (X, Y, Z) is tied to a specific directory group. Any human or AI reading this file must bump EXACTLY the number indicated by the 'rules' list below, based on which directory changed (if several groups changed in the same commit, the rule with the highest priority, i.e. the lowest 'bump_index', is applied, and the positions below it are reset).
versioning_policy.instructions_for_ai: When updating the version manually or automatically: 1) Determine which 'watched_paths' group each changed file belongs to. 2) Among the matching rules, pick the one with the lowest 'bump_index' (i.e. the highest-priority change). 3) Increment the position named in that rule's 'bump' field (x/y/z) by 1. 4) Reset every position after it to 0 (since 'reset_lower' is true). 5) Update 'version' and 'previous_version' accordingly and append a new entry to 'changelog'.

rules.description: Any change in modules/ (scanner, host, detection, etc.) increments X (major) by 1; Y and Z are reset to 0.
Any change in signatures/ or rules/ increments Y (minor) by 1; Z is reset to 0. (If modules/ changed in the same commit, the bump_index=1 rule takes precedence.)
Any change in core/ increments Z (patch) by 1. Applies only when the higher-priority groups (modules/, signatures/, rules/) have no changes.

versioning_policy.automation: This policy is applied automatically by the version_checker.py script; it runs silently in the background every time the tool (oxport.py) starts, comparing the current directory state against the previous scan stored in .version_state.json.

changes: core/exporter.py: tightened the --live --cidr host table column widths (TARGET 16, STATUS 11, matching the existing port table's proportions) to remove the excess whitespace between TARGET/STATUS/TYPE

modules/host/discovery.py: discover_hosts() and discover_hosts_ranged() now accept an on_start callback, fired after all planning/info log lines (target count, chunk split, per-thread range) but right before the actual probing begins

core/engine.py: the --live host table header is now passed to discover_hosts()/discover_hosts_ranged() as on_start instead of being printed up front, so it renders immediately above the first live row instead of above the discovery log lines
bumped per the versioning_policy's 'modules/' rule (highest priority), which also resets Y and Z to 0

core/exporter.py: reworked the --live --cidr host table to TARGET / STATUS / TYPE columns (STATUS shows 'LIVE', TYPE shows the discovery method in upper case, e.g. 'ICMP'); dropped the HOSTNAME column

modules/host/discovery.py: added discover_hosts_ranged(), splitting a target list into N contiguous, non-overlapping chunks (one dedicated thread per chunk via split_into_ranges) instead of a plain thread pool, mirroring the existing ranged port-scan logic

core/engine.py: --cidr now always stops after host discovery and never runs a port scan, regardless of --ports/-A/--syn/etc.; this replaces the previous behavior where only --ping-only skipped port scanning

core/engine.py: when --cidr is combined with --threads N, discovery now uses the new ranged splitting (e.g. a /24 with --threads 2 gives thread 1 the first 127 hosts and thread 2 the next 127 hosts, with no overlap) instead of a shared thread pool

core/exporter.py: added print_live_hosts_header() and print_live_host() so --live prints each discovered host as soon as it is found, bumped per the versioning_policy's 'modules/' rule (highest priority), which also resets Y and Z to 0

Replaced the nmap-style txt output (Host: ip / PORT STATE SERVICE) with a custom TARGET / PORT / STATUS / GUESS table layout, with status labels renamed (open -> reachable, closed -> unreachable, filtered -> no-response, unfiltered -> unreachable)
Expanded signatures/port_name.json from 26 to 167 TCP entries and from 13 to 47 UDP entries
Added --os {windows,linux} flag that restricts a scan to ports typically associated with the chosen OS
Added signatures/windows.json and signatures/linux.json OS-specific port signature files
Added core/os_profiles.py to load OS port profiles and classify a port as windows-only, linux-only, shared by both, or neither
Added ANSI color output to the txt exporter: target IP in bright blue, port number in bright orange, reachable status in bright green
Colored the GUESS column by OS relevance: windows-only ports in light blue, linux-only ports in bright pink, ports shared by both OS profiles in purple, and unmatched ports in gray
Colors are automatically disabled when output is not a terminal (redirected to a file) or when the NO_COLOR environment variable is set

Added support for combining --all-ports with --threads N: the full 1-65535 port range is split into N contiguous chunks, each scanned by its own dedicated worker thread, instead of one thread per individual port
Added --live flag: each open port is printed to the console immediately as it is discovered, instead of only after the whole scan finishes
Consolidated all Python bytecode caches into a single pycache/ folder at the project root (via sys.pycache_prefix in oxport.py), instead of a __pycache__ folder appearing in every package directory
Renamed the service-version-detection flag's long form from -V/--version to -V/--service-version to free up --version for the tool's own version flag
Added --version flag that prints the current project version, read from this version.json file
Initial version of oxport as provided by the user
